requirements.text: Lat/lon projection round-trips and matches great-circle distance within 0.3%.
Sun position matches SF solar noon, sunrise and night; drives day/night.
Progress persists, survives broken storage, and round-trips through a share code.
Drone flight: cruise/boost speeds, turning, ground/water/ceiling limits, wall bounce, battery, wind.
Building footprints parse, collide (walls and roofs), honor exclusions, and mesh with correct facing.
Shipped city and terrain data cover the whole city with real heights and hills.
Keyboard, gamepad and touch merge into flight axes; actions fire once; typing never flies the drone.
Every activity is valid, unique, inside SF bounds, with real prerequisites and no cycles.
Every activity kind validates params and has a label and icon.
Activities start, lock, complete, fail on time, grant XP and cards exactly once.
The game boots the whole city with zero console errors and draws to the screen.
Real keyboard input flies the drone forward, up and around.
The drone cannot pass through buildings at full boost.
Every menu panel opens, renders and closes without errors.
HUD and menus render on iPad and phone with no horizontal overflow.
On-screen sticks fly the drone on touch devices.
First-run onboarding teaches the controls, shows once, and can be skipped.
Settings (quality, units, volume, reduced motion, controls) persist across reloads.
The map shows the player and activities and sets a waypoint the HUD follows.
The collection book lists every card, with locked cards shown as mysteries.
Menus have no serious or critical axe accessibility violations and are keyboard navigable.
Installable PWA: valid manifest, 192/512 icons, service worker registers.
Every activity in the game can be completed by the automated solver.
At least 150 non-discovery activities across at least 12 kinds.
Every card referenced exists; every card has real lore, a category and a source.
The main quest completes chapter by chapter with clues revealed in order.
The daily clue is deterministic per calendar date and solvable.
Photo mode captures a shot and photo challenges score framing.
Every minigame kind can be won and lost, and records a best score.
At least 15 hand-built landmark models exist, sit at verified coordinates, and collide.
Post-2010 towers (Salesforce Tower and others) are present at their real heights.
Two players in the same room see each other move.
A map ping from one player appears for the other.
Text chat is delivered between players and is length-limited and escaped.
Multiplayer modes (race, tag, hide-and-seek in fog) start, score and finish.
Proximity voice: one spatial audio node per peer, volume falls with distance, mute works.
Share links carry a room code and opening one joins that room.
A sync code moves progress from one device to another.
Every live data feed has an offline fallback; the game boots with the network blocked.
Weather and fog feeds parse real fixtures and drive fog density and wind.
Audio starts only after a user gesture, mixes ambience and music, and mute persists.
Ask-the-City uses handwritten lore offline and the Cloudflare proxy only when configured.
Initial JS stays under the gzip budget and the city is ready within 30s in CI.
A scripted 60-second tour across the city produces zero console errors.
